reason: Next.js MCP route registers two implemented GA4 read tools using Google Analytics Admin and Data clients with per-user OAuth refresh tokens.

tools.name: list_properties
tools.description: Lists GA4 properties YOU have access to. Pass user=<your-email>.
tools.behavior: Loads google_refresh:<user> from Redis, constructs an AnalyticsAdminServiceClient with authorized-user OAuth credentials and REST fallback, calls listAccountSummaries({}), flattens all returned propertySummaries to account display name, property display name, and propertyId with properties/ removed, and returns pretty-printed JSON in text content. Catches errors and returns diagnostic text with isError true.
notes: The user string has no email-format constraint; it is a Redis refresh-token lookup identifier.

tools.name: run_report
tools.description: Runs a GA4 report as the specified user.
tools.behavior: Loads the selected user OAuth refresh token from Redis and calls BetaAnalyticsDataClient.runReport with property properties/<propertyId>, one date range, metrics mapped to name objects, dimensions mapped to name objects (empty when omitted), and the limit (default 100). Returns the entire API response as pretty-printed JSON text. Catches errors and returns diagnostic text with isError true.
notes: Schema accepts unrestricted strings for dates and propertyId and allows empty metric/dimension arrays; GA API validity is not checked locally.
The registration exposes only these report fields, not an arbitrary full runReport request.
Source review only; no upstream execution, tools/list request, or live API requests.
Both tools register unconditionally in the sole createMcpHandler callback. The HTTP endpoint requires a bearer token equal to MCP_BEARER_TOKEN via withMcpAuth(required: true).

Deployment requires Upstash Redis environment configuration, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI, and MCP_BEARER_TOKEN; each selected user must have an OAuth refresh token in Redis. Google OAuth start/callback routes request analytics.readonly and store the token; these HTTP routes are not MCP tools.

Input schemas reconstructed from explicit Zod registration shapes. additionalProperties false represents the default Zod object conversion; unknown keys are stripped by default validation, rather than a custom strict() constraint.
No definite entrypoint blocker found by source inspection.

review.method: Independently reconstructed both inline Zod schemas and descriptions exactly with a TypeScript AST; read both handlers, user-specific Google clients and bearer wrapper. No extra tool modules exist.
